NAFR  HIGH COURT OF CHHATTISGARH AT BILASPUR  MCRC No. 5383 of 2024 1.
Dinesh Yadav @ Bijul S/o Shri Jagdish Prasad Aged About 37 Years R/o Village Bhalaur, Police Station Manendragarh, District Manendragarh Chirmiri Bharatpur (C.G.)
... Petitioners  versus 1. State Of Chhattisgarh Through Police Station Manendragarh, District Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur (C.G.)
... Respondents For Applicant : Mr. Shrawan Agrawal, Advocate For State : Mr. Shreyansh Mehta, Panel Lawyer (Hon'ble Shri Parth Prateem Sahu, Judge) Order on Board 13/08/2024 1.

Applicant has filed this second bail application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail as he was arrested in connection with Crime No. 83 of 2024 registered at Police Station Manendragarh, District Manendragarh-Chirmiri-Bharatpur (C.G.) for offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C., 1860.
2.
Case of the prosecution, in brief, is that, on 20.04.2024 applicant took victim on his motor-cycle on the pretext that he will get Aadhar Card of victim updated.

He took her to his shop and after verifying from computer he informed victim that amount of Mahatari Vandan Yojana has been transferred in her account and thereafter took victim to drop her to her house.
Instead of taking victim to her house, he took her to lonely place, brought liquor, forcefully administered liquor to her and committed forceful sexual intercourse with her.
Incident was reported to the concerned Police Station, based on the report, aforementioned crime was registered against applicant and he was arrested on 24.03.2024.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent, he has not committed any offence as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the aforementioned crime.
Victim has now been examined before learned Trial Court, applicant is in jail since 24.03.2024, hence, he may be enlarged on regular bail.

4. Learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for applicant and would submit that there are specific allegation against applicant of committing forceful sexual intercourse with victim.
In the Court deposition also, victim has supported the case.
5. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

6. Considering facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation, age of victim, submission made by learned counsel for respective parties, victim is now examined before learned Trial Court on 09.07.2024 and hence, there is no apprehension of influencing material witnesses, trial may take some time for its conclusion, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to enlarge applicant on regular bail 7.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail, upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court on the conditions that - (a) Applicant shall appear before the Trial Court regularly on each and every date,
unless exempted from appearance.
( b) The applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
(c) If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
(Parth Prateem Sahu) JUDGE Shayna Dinesh Yadav @ Bijul vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 13 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178469414/
